name: price-tier
description: One plan in a set of plans. A price, its terms, and what you get — and the composition rule that four equal tiers are four tiers the eye lands nowhere in, so one of them is `featured` and the rest are quiet. On the site each tier was a card, a hand-built price line and a bare `<ul>` with `space-y-1.5`, repeated per tier with the amount and the caption re-typed at three different sizes.

amount.$description: Tabular, always. Prices in a row that do not share digit widths do not line up, and a set of tiers is read by comparing exactly this number.

action.$description: `margin-block-start: auto` pins it to the bottom, so a row of tiers with different feature counts still lines its buttons up. Without it the eye compares three buttons at three heights instead of three prices.

featured.$description: ONE tier in the set. Four equal tiers is four tiers the eye lands nowhere in — the lead has to be visibly the lead, or the page has no recommendation and the reader has to do the work.

a11y.note: The features are a real `<ul>`, which is what announces 'list, six items' — a set of `<div>`s reads as running prose and gives no count. The featured tier is not marked by colour alone: it carries a badge saying why, because 'the one with the gold border' is not information a screen reader has.
